items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Anyway, that was the first and last lesson that I had from Jack Smith.

ctx.x: same "Sophisticated Lady" himself on the piano, and the way he played it just seemed to make an impression. I always feel like that particular moment was what made me realize that I wanted to play the piano more than anything in my life. I still didn't think of myself playing it as a profession or a livelihood. Before it had been something that I did, and I did it between baseball and football, and playing out with other kids -- it was just something that I could do. But when I heard this, I just felt like there…

So, if I can digress a little bit, oh, about six or seven months after my uncle and my father brought this piano to the house, I had been coming in every evening, sitting and playing, and no one ever had to tell me to practice or anything like that. So they just let me play as much as I wanted to. And my mother was always very encouraging. And my father decided he would give me piano lessons. Well, there was a fellow, one of the friends of my father that used to come around, and he would play for little…
